title: Linus Torvalds: "Tell Your AI Companion To Get Its Act Together"
byline: Written by Michael Larabel in Linux Storage on 24 November 2026 at 04:01 PM EST. 49 Comments
excerpt: A big EXT4 pull request today intended for the Linux 7.4-rc5 kernel has set off Linus Torvalds
content_html:
A big EXT4 pull request today intended for the Linux 7.4-rc5 kernel has set off Linus Torvalds. Over 41k lines of new code in this EXT4 pull request going in as "fixes".... Much of that being new KUnit test coverage to make it safer to validate AI-generated patches. And then a lot of AI generated patches themselves for the EXT4 file-system.

Sent in today was the latest EXT4 pull request for the ongoing Linux 7.4 cycle. There are some interesting performance changes while the vast majority of the code in this big "fixes" pull request were AI generated bug fixes and expanding the KUnit test coverage of the EXT4 driver to help in validating future AI generated patches.

But this massive pull request coming in at the back-half of the Linux 7.4 cycle is much to Linus Torvalds' displeasure. He ended up honoring the pull request and is now merged, but he remarked on the kernel mailing list:

"Honestly, I don't think this was appropriate for this stage. You should have kept your tests in a separate branch for your testing, and done this *huge* update for the next merge window.

This whole notion of "anything that is a fix goes in -rc" is bogus.

I've taken this, despite serious reservations and some bad conflicts due to this braindamage.

But next time this kind of sh*t happens I'll just ignore it.

STOP THINKING THAT YOU - OR AI - NEVER ADD BUGS WHEN YOU FIX SOMETHING.

There's a why we have release candidates and several weeks of calming things down.

Yes, I'm pissed off. Why the he** people have such a hard time understanding such a simple concept is hard to understand.

If you think that "41197 insertions" is ok and cannot introduce new problems just because most of it won't be compiled or becasue they were fixes for other things, you are full of crap.

If the bugs were subtle things that have been around for a while without being detected by AI, the fixes by definition are fixing something subtle and rare that nobody has noticed until now.

And that makes the *fixes* possibly buggy.

I was going to just unpull it, but I dealt with this and am giving you a fair warning instead. Get your sh*t together and stop this kind of idiocy.

And tell your AI companion to get its act together, and do any new development and test-cases ON A SEPARATE DA*N BRANCH, so that it can be merged during the MERGE WINDOW.

What's so hard to understand about this?

And yes, it will mean that *you* have to deal with the resulting conflicts while running those tests, but dam*it, it will also mean that we don't introduce tens of thousands of lines of random crap in the middle of a release!

Linus"

So the EXT4 changes are in for Sunday's Linux 7.4-rc5 kernel release, but Torvalds is not happy.

When it comes to the performance work, one of the interesting items is spreading the inodes of files in sibling directories over the block groups of a flex group. Ultimately this helps reduce contention and can significantly speed-up parallel file creation. The patch from Samsung's Daejun Park shows some very nice improvements:

Separately are also performance patches to improve unlink performance on file-systems without the orphan file feature and also speeding up fast commit replay on sparse files.
